recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It removes a misleading active terminology definition while preserving later work-group decisions about the distinction between direct Reference.identifier searches and chained searches.
issue_request: FHIR-14103 was Published as Persuasive with Modification for STU3. It requested a :identifier modifier for reference searches that matches Reference.identifier and clarification that chaining, reverse chaining, and includes are defined for resolvable reference values rather than logical-only identifiers.
initial_application: Git-svn commit 50ab308d337b68e176336b281e7179a935140d7a, corresponding to SVN revision 13428, applied the issue to source/search.html by adding :identifier prose and examples. Later search-page work preserved and refined the rule, but the later extracted search-modifier-code CodeSystem retained a conflicting identifier concept definition.
additional_context: FHIR-29410 and FHIR-37424 confirmed that :identifier and .identifier chaining are intentionally distinct: :identifier matches Reference.identifier, while .identifier searches the resolved referenced resource. FHIR-43073 and FHIR-45252 later clarified reference search type, canonical, chaining, include, and reverse-include language; those related issues are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Updated source/searchparameter/codesystem-search-modifier-code.xml so the identifier concept definition says the modifier applies to Reference.identifier instead of Reference.reference. No source/search.html change was needed because the current narrative already carries the correct rule and later FHIR-45252 wording.
source_changes: source/searchparameter/codesystem-search-modifier-code.xml: changed the search-modifier-code identifier concept definition from a generic resource-identifier statement to explicit Reference.identifier versus Reference.reference wording.
